coordinatorSummary: CONSENT at 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with no advisories. Ten attacks run, none landed. Custody holds: subject 1cab6a1f at 0444 unmoved with dispatch and prompt agreeing, HEAD never left 5537d60, file 08 at 3a9442d1 and COORD at 11887824 both matching the draft's pins, no D-166 heading, C-D166 unused. The duplicate is real: exactly two ## D-165 headings occur, and both commits the draft names, 47ab93c then 5537d60 with identical titles, resolve in git. The one thing that matters in a deletion act is whether the copy being deleted carries anything the kept copy does not, and that is the assertion a reviewer must not take on trust, so I diffed the two recitals myself. Keep-first is right by a wide margin. Recital 2 drops three substantive elements recital 1 has: the full DR-125 limbs reading 'OBL-DR125-ACTIVATION rides DR-125; D-110 binds NOTHING. Matrix authoring waits on DR-125 closure or disposition' where recital 2 has a bare 'DR-125'; the Rust-as-core refusal; and D-110's place in the reversibility list. Recital 2's only two unique strings are a branch-list word, '/ D-162', which deviates from the frozen D-165 draft that recital 1 matches exactly, and a 'retarget DR-125' refusal whose substance recital 1 carries affirmatively and more strongly. So the deletion loses nothing material, and it restores fidelity to the frozen draft. Both recitals cite the same frozen subject and the same two CONSENT verdicts, all of which reproduce at 0444, so neither rests on evidence the other lacks. The act keeps the surviving recital byte-unchanged, refuses to rewrite D-165's Decision, refuses to union the extra branch-list words, and leaves readiness at zero with condition 2 at 4 of 32 and condition 4 MET at 26 of 26. Two items are recorded as considered and declined. The precedent citation is exact for D-087, whose heading is literally 'Remove the duplicate D-056 heading', and loose for D-156, where the correction was a hygiene commit rather than the numbered entry — git shows the same shape at D-144 and D-139 — but that difference favours this act, which is putting the same operation through a full adversarial cycle instead of a bare commit. I also record the full recital diff in this verdict so you can see precisely what the deletion removes rather than relying on either of our characterisations.
